title.title: The complete Crouzeix conjecture: the constant is 2
title.subtitle: Claim: $\|P(A)\| \le 2 \sup_{W(A)} \|P\|$ for every Hilbert-space operator $A$, even with matrix coefficients

plain: A matrix's 'numerical range' controls its polynomials up to a factor 2, even with matrix coefficients

beats.text: $A = \begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$: spectrum $\{0\}$, numerical range a disk of radius $1/2$
Crouzeix (2004): $W(A)$ controls $p(A)$ up to a factor 2; this $A$ shows 2 is sharp
The scalar case fell to humans this summer. The claim is the complete form

steps: Expand the Cauchy kernel in Faber polynomials
A positive kernel keeps each coefficient between weights 1 and 2
Compare two orderings, so matrix coefficients never commute

after.label: Claimed, Sep 2026

sources.quote: Crouzeix conjectured in 2004 that for any square matrix $A$ and polynomial $p$, $\|p(A)\| \le 2 \max_{W(A)} |p|$, where $W(A)$ is the numerical range.
Crouzeix-Palencia (SIAM J. Matrix Anal. Appl. 38, 2017) gave 1+sqrt2, also completely bounded
||P[A]|| <= 2 sup_{z in W(A)} ||P(z)||; i.e. the closure of the numerical range is a complete 2-spectral set; constant 2 sharp (2x2 nilpotent)
Complete version proved for base matrices of order <= 3 by Ahag-Czyz-Virtanen, arXiv:2608.27346 (Aug/Sep 2026)
The headline 'Crouzeix conjecture' (scalar) was solved by humans+AI in July-Aug 2026, ~2 months before this release
Solution modules (~39k lines across Analysis/DirectCrouzeix, NumericalRange, Crouzeix, StructuralCrouzeix, HilbertCrouzeix)
